sense: the power or manner of speaking

terms.gloss: speech, the power of speaking; a way of speaking
evidence: Cic. Off. 1.50: ejus autem vinculum est ratiō et ōrātiō
Cic. Off. 1.12: ad ōrātiōnis et ad vītae societātem
terms.comment: Lewis & Short: “speech, the power or faculty of speech, the habit or use of language”. With reason it is what sets people apart from animals, which are ratiōnis et ōrātiōnis expertēs (Off. 1.50). Also a person’s way of speaking.

phrases.latin: ejus autem vinculum est ratiō et ōrātiō, quae docendō, discendō, commūnicandō, disceptandō, jūdicandō conciliat inter sē hominēs conjungitque nātūrālī quādam societāte
phrases.english: and its bond is reason and speech, which by teaching, learning, sharing, debating and judging bring people together and join them in a kind of natural fellowship

phrases.latin: ex ejus linguā melle dulcior fluēbat ōrātiō
phrases.english: speech sweeter than honey flowed from his tongue

sources: Quotations from the Latinitas loci collections (loci-cicero-philosophica), as checked there against the editions they name.
